title: List the products
prompt: Show each category and its product names joined with commas, in name order, as names. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT category, GROUP_CONCAT(name ORDER BY name) AS names FROM products GROUP BY category;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT category, GROUP_CONCAT(name ORDER BY name DESC) AS names FROM products GROUP BY category;
SELECT category, COUNT(name) AS names FROM products GROUP BY category;

title: A custom separator
prompt: Show each department_id and its employee names separated by a semicolon and a space, in name order, as team.
hints: The separator is the second value.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT department_id, GROUP_CONCAT(name, '; ' ORDER BY name) AS team FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department_id, GROUP_CONCAT(name ORDER BY name) AS team FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;
SELECT department_id, GROUP_CONCAT(name, ', ' ORDER BY name) AS team FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

title: Remove repeats
prompt: Show each user_id and the different devices they used, joined with commas in alphabetical order, as devices.
hints: DISTINCT goes first inside the brackets.
solutions: SELECT user_id, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT device ORDER BY device) AS devices FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT user_id, GROUP_CONCAT(device ORDER BY device) AS devices FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id;
SELECT user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT device) AS devices FROM sessions GROUP BY user_id;

title: A course's students
prompt: Show each course_id and its student_ids joined with a dash, in ascending order, as roster. Repeats can stay.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT course_id, GROUP_CONCAT(student_id, '-' ORDER BY student_id) AS roster FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT course_id, GROUP_CONCAT(student_id ORDER BY student_id) AS roster FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id;
SELECT course_id, GROUP_CONCAT(student_id, '-' ORDER BY student_id DESC) AS roster FROM enrolments GROUP BY course_id;

title: NULLs are skipped
prompt: Show each department_id and its known emails in order, joined with commas, as emails. Missing emails are simply left out.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT department_id, GROUP_CONCAT(email ORDER BY email) AS emails FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department_id, GROUP_CONCAT(COALESCE(email, 'none') ORDER BY email) AS emails FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;
SELECT department_id, COUNT(email) AS emails FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

title: Fix the syntax
prompt: This should list each category's names with a slash between them, in name order, as names. It uses MySQL's SEPARATOR word, which SQLite doesn't support. Fix it.
starterSql:
SELECT category,
  GROUP_CONCAT(name ORDER BY name SEPARATOR '/') AS names
FROM products
GROUP BY category;
hints: In SQLite, the separator is just the second value.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT category, GROUP_CONCAT(name, '/' ORDER BY name) AS names FROM products GROUP BY category;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT category, GROUP_CONCAT(name ORDER BY name) AS names FROM products GROUP BY category;
SELECT category, GROUP_CONCAT(name, '/') AS names FROM products WHERE 1 = 0 GROUP BY category;

title: Order contents
prompt: Show each order_id and its product names in alphabetical order, joined with a comma and a space, as contents.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT i.order_id, GROUP_CONCAT(p.name, ', ' ORDER BY p.name) AS contents FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY i.order_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT i.order_id, GROUP_CONCAT(i.product_id, ', ' ORDER BY p.name) AS contents FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY i.order_id;
SELECT i.order_id, GROUP_CONCAT(p.name, ',' ORDER BY p.name) AS contents FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY i.order_id;

title: Daily summary
prompt: Show each session_date, how many different users were active as users, and their user_ids in order with no repeats as user_list, sorted by date.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (15, 7, '2024-02-28', 5, 'ios');

solutions: SELECT session_date, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS users, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT user_id ORDER BY user_id) AS user_list FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date ORDER BY session_date;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT session_date, COUNT(user_id) AS users, GROUP_CONCAT(user_id ORDER BY user_id) AS user_list FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date ORDER BY session_date;
SELECT session_date, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS users, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT user_id ORDER BY user_id) AS user_list FROM sessions GROUP BY session_date ORDER BY session_date DESC;
